title: Commercial litigation
summary: Contract, partnership and business-tort disputes in state and federal court, from the demand letter through trial. Most of our cases end before trial; all of them are prepared as if they will not.
body:
Commercial cases are won or lost on documents. In the first thirty days we collect the contracts, the emails and the invoices, put them on one timeline, and tell you in writing what we think the case is worth and what it will cost to find out.

Early case assessment

Every new matter gets a short written assessment: the claims and defenses, the three facts that matter most, a budget by phase, and the settlement range we would recommend if the other side offered it tomorrow. We update it at each phase.

Trial

Two partners in this group have tried cases to verdict in the (fictional) Wendlow County Circuit Court within the last three years. When a case should be tried, we say so early.
scope: Breach of contract and warranty|Partnership and shareholder disputes|Business torts and unfair competition|Injunctions and temporary restraining orders|Collection of commercial judgments
refer: Securities class actions|Patent litigation|Criminal matters (we refer to defense counsel we trust)
fee_note: Hourly, billed monthly by phase against a written budget; alternative fees on request
steps: Assess :: A written assessment of claims, defenses, budget and settlement range within 30 days.||Plead :: Complaint or answer, early motions, and a litigation hold sent to the right people.||Discover :: Documents, depositions and experts, run against the phase budget.||Resolve :: Mediation, summary judgment or trial, with your decision at each fork.

title: Appeals
summary: Appeals and post-trial motions in state and federal appellate courts, including cases tried by other firms. We also consult with trial teams before a verdict to preserve issues.
body:
An appeal is a different case from the trial: a closed record, a standard of review, and a few pages to make the point. We read the whole record before we say whether an appeal is worth taking.

Before the verdict

Trial teams bring us in to draft jury instructions, frame objections and protect the record, so the issues exist if an appeal is needed.
scope: Civil appeals in state and federal court|Post-trial motions|Issue preservation during trial|Amicus briefs for trade associations
fee_note: Flat fee by stage (record review, brief, argument), quoted in writing
steps: Record :: Read the full record and write a one-page merits memo.||Brief :: Opening brief, reply, and appendix.||Argue :: Moots with the team, then oral argument.

title: Employment disputes
summary: Advice and litigation for employers and executives: restrictive covenants, wage claims, discrimination charges and separation agreements.
body:
Most employment disputes start with a phone call on a Friday afternoon: a resignation to a competitor, a demand letter, an agency charge. We answer that call, and then we help you decide whether the dispute is worth having.

For employers

Agency charges, wage-and-hour claims, non-compete enforcement, and handbook and policy reviews.

For executives

Employment agreements, separation terms and restrictive covenant reviews before you sign or resign.
scope: Non-compete and trade secret disputes|Agency charges and investigations|Wage and hour claims|Executive agreements and separations
fee_note: Flat fee for agreement reviews; hourly for disputes
steps: Call :: Same-day call on urgent matters, with a conflict check first.||Contain :: Preserve evidence, send or answer the letter, set the timeline.||Decide :: Negotiate, mediate or litigate, with a written budget.

title: Construction disputes
summary: Payment, delay and defect disputes for owners, contractors and design professionals, including mechanic's liens and arbitration.
body:
Construction disputes are about schedules and money. We read the contract, the change orders and the daily logs before anything else, and we work with scheduling experts when delay is the issue.

Liens and deadlines

Lien and notice deadlines are short and strict. If you are owed money on a project, call before the deadline, not after.
scope: Mechanic's liens and payment bond claims|Delay and disruption claims|Construction defect claims|Arbitration under industry contracts
fee_note: Hourly; lien filings at a flat fee
steps: Notice :: Check notice and lien deadlines on day one.||Assemble :: Contract, change orders, logs and schedule into one file.||Resolve :: Negotiate, arbitrate or litigate.

title: Business formation and governance
summary: Entities, operating agreements, board work and the governance questions that come up as a company grows or changes hands.
body:
Most disputes we litigate started as a governance document nobody read. We write operating agreements and bylaws that say what happens when partners disagree, someone wants out, or someone dies.

For boards

Board minutes, conflict-of-interest policies and special committee work for privately held companies and nonprofits.
scope: Entity formation and conversions|Operating agreements and bylaws|Buy-sell agreements|Board and special committee counsel
refer: Public company securities filings|Tax opinions (we work with your CPA)
fee_note: Flat fees for formation packages; hourly for governance counsel
steps: Listen :: A first meeting about the people, not the paperwork.||Draft :: Documents in plain English with a cover memo.||Maintain :: Annual review of minutes, filings and ownership.

title: Contracts and commercial transactions
summary: Supply, services, licensing and distribution agreements, negotiated so the dispute clause is never needed.
body: We draft and negotiate the agreements a growing company signs every month. Each contract goes back to you with a one-page summary: what you agreed to, what you can walk away from, and what to calendar.
scope: Supply and distribution agreements|Master services agreements|Software and data licensing|Asset purchases
fee_note: Flat fee per template; hourly for negotiations
steps: Scope :: Learn the deal and the walk-away points.||Draft :: Mark up in tracked changes with comments that explain why.||Close :: Signature, summary and a calendar of obligations.

title: Trademarks and brand protection
summary: Clearance, registration and enforcement for names, logos and product lines.
body: A name is easier to clear than to defend. We search before you print, register what matters, and send the letter when someone else uses your mark.
scope: Clearance searches|Federal trademark applications|Cease-and-desist letters|Domain name disputes
fee_note: Flat fees for searches and applications
steps: Search :: Knock-out and full clearance searches.||File :: Application, office actions and registration.||Watch :: Monitoring and enforcement letters.

title: Estate planning and probate
summary: Wills, trusts, powers of attorney and probate administration for families and business owners.
body:
An estate plan is a set of instructions for a hard week. We write plans that the people you name can actually follow, and we sit down with them if you ask us to.

Probate

When someone dies, we guide the personal representative through the Wendlow County probate court one step at a time, with a checklist that shows what is done and what is next.
scope: Wills and revocable trusts|Powers of attorney and health care directives|Probate and trust administration|Succession plans for family businesses
fee_note: Flat fees for plans; hourly for administration
steps: Inventory :: What you own and how it is titled.||Decide :: Who decides, who inherits, and when.||Sign :: A signing meeting with witnesses and a binder.

title: Real estate
summary: Commercial leases, purchases, zoning and title questions for owners, tenants and lenders.
body: We review leases and purchase agreements for the terms that cost money later: assignment, repairs, renewal options and default. Zoning and title questions get a written answer with the map attached.
scope: Commercial leases|Purchases and sales|Zoning and land use|Title objections
fee_note: Flat fee for lease reviews; hourly for transactions
steps: Review :: Term sheet and title.||Negotiate :: Lease or contract mark-up.||Close :: Closing checklist and recorded documents.
